findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: identify, check_service_endpoint, preflight_payment, evaluate_action, test_purchase, knock_on_endpoint, list_x402_endpoints · Private data: identify, check_service_endpoint, preflight_payment, vault_assessment, vault_exits, vault_risk_dimensions, portfolio_screen, capital_coverage, exit_lifecycle_coverage, endpoint_coverage, payment_evidence, evaluate_action, test_purchase, knock_on_endpoint, counterparty_check, vault_check, find_vaults, operator_check, list_vaults, find_agents, counterparty_history, vaults_earned, agent_changes, counterparty_bulk, agent_business, agent_economic_profile, exit_screen, vault_exit_confidence, check_action, inspect_payment, record_receipt, monitor_subject · Public sink: vault_assessment, vault_exits, portfolio_screen, test_purchase, knock_on_endpoint, find_vaults, operator_check, vaults_earned, agent_business, exit_screen, vault_exit_confidence, check_action · Destructive: preflight_payment, vault_assessment, vault_risk_dimensions, list_policies, agent_business, check_action, monitor_subject.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
